title: Security fault matrix
description: Objective: run hostile credentials, stale authority, command replay, corruption, crash-at-boundary, poison, resource, and provider fault schedules across the full system. Deliverable: security/fault fixtures and exact evidence. NOT in scope: host-malicious sandbox claims. Hard dependencies: Schedule coverage checker and all production adapters. Owned paths: tests/security/** and tests/fault/**. Verification: pnpm test:fault && pnpm test:security.
definitionOfDone: Every declared authority and external-effect boundary has hostile before/after/race coverage.
No unauthorized mutation, duplicate effect, budget mint, hidden skip, or false evidence acceptance occurs.
Unobservable host behavior is labeled outside-scope or UNKNOWN precisely.
taskRails: Claims follow the benchmark permit-list; missing, partial, cross-basis, or unverifiable evidence is UNKNOWN, never PASS.
No confirmatory corpus is generated or viewed until the implementation commit is frozen exactly as specified.
GO_QUIESCE and GO_ACTIVATE are separate human decisions. Keep evidence exact, reproducible, and scoped to one source commit.

This task is also too broad for one <=60-minute implementation slice once its production subjects exist: the committed tree currently exposes at least eight security surfaces and eight fault surfaces. Re-plan it as the FINAL integration/hardening proof after these file-disjoint test slices land:

1. Authority transport hostile matrix — tests/security/transports/**. Drive public production ingress for daemon HTTP/event stream, MCP stdio/Streamable HTTP, authenticated IDE/control-room, importer, and force paths. Case rows cover missing/malformed/expired/revoked/swapped/replayed credentials and stale version/epoch/binding/command/artifact identities. Each row pins exact stable code AND refusing layer/stage and reads authoritative state/effect/budget/audit deltas back as zero. Generated rows assert non-zero count and exact set equality with the production registry.
2. Integrity/scope hostile matrix — tests/security/integrity/**. Drive production path/scope, symlink/junction/submodule/UNC/device/case, malicious Git ref, argv/env, N/N+1 bounds, provider-closure swap, evidence substitution/tamper, redaction and distribution handshake surfaces. Same code/layer and zero-authority assertions; same production-registry non-vacuity ratchet.
3. Durable-store fault matrix — tests/fault/store/**. Real SQLite/subprocess schedules at transaction begin/write/commit/ack, WAL/checkpoint, corruption/permission/lock, outbox/inbox/projection poison and replay. Assert whole-or-none durable truth, exact STORE/OUTBOX code+layer, command replay idempotency, no lost acknowledged event, and no duplicate delivery. Test-produced helpers must not replace relay/controller production entry points.
4. Runtime/provider fault matrix — tests/fault/runtime/**. Drive production dispatcher/supervisor/platform/provider/resource/budget/artifact composition before/after/race at registration, lock, activation, physical start, result, ack, cancel and recovery. Assert one authoritative effect, no budget mint/slot/resource duplication, exact recovery/refusal code+layer, and honest UNKNOWN for unobservable host facts. Host-malicious same-user behavior is explicitly OUTSIDE_SCOPE, never PASS or skip.
5. Gate-lane wiring prerequisite — root package.json plus tests/fault/tsconfig.json and tests/security/tsconfig.json. Shell-neutral scripts must run strict tsc over all tests/** lane files before Vitest: pnpm test:fault and pnpm test:security. Root recursive typecheck does not cover tests/** today.

This task then owns the full-matrix ratchet and final proof only: verify every prerequisite shipping task is DONE and reachable from a real consumer, exact design/benchmark hashes and one source commit, no confirmatory corpus bytes, exhaustive production registry ↔ executed-case set equality, exact UNKNOWN/outside-scope rows, and one adversarial mutation per refusal layer plus one deleted-case non-vacuity mutation.

comments.author: architect-5b5302ee
comments.content:
Third planning pass: exact prerequisite probes, case contract, oracles, and mutation plan. This extends the handoff only; governor msg-a973ed5907cc4925943b8d7a6a67e885 explicitly says the unknown PLANNING flip did not resolve the block.

A. Re-plan admission checklist — every row must be true at one committed source SHA before submitting the parent plan:
1. Daemon authority composition: a non-test production caller binds core authenticateCommand, daemon buildCommandRegistry/handleCommandRequest, and SqliteEventStore/decision application. Today authenticateCommand and handleCommandRequest have test-only callers and handleCommandRequest is absent from the daemon root.
2. Event transport composition: readEventPage/resumeFromSnapshot are behind authenticated byte/listener ingress and a real SubscriptionPort; today they are root-exported kernels with no auth/listener composition.
3. MCP composition: @moe/mcp root exposes both stable stdio and Streamable HTTP entry points and production StdioDispatchPort/HttpDispatchPort/HttpSessionPort implementations call the daemon. Today HTTP internals are sealed and both transports rely on injected ports.
4. Import composition: applyImport is reachable from an authenticated daemon/CLI command over a copied frozen source plus a real store transaction; today only package tests consume it.
5. Control-room/IDE composition: production main mounts createDataAdapter with a real DaemonTransport/session/event stream, and the JetBrains adapter is landed; today main mounts fixture state and adapters/ is absent.
6. Force/R3 composition: durable authenticated handlers exist for lease.confirm_revoke, resource.confirm_released, budget.conservative_settle, budget.acknowledge_unknown_liability, recovery.complete and cutover commands, enforcing recent step-up and reason; today vocabulary/builders/doctor proposals are zero-authority shapes.
7. Store relay composition: relayMessage is public and has a durable production consumer; today it is package-internal and consumed only by tests/drill helpers.
8. Effect/platform composition: a production dispatcher calls activateEffect, consumes/validates the one-use grant, registers an OS lock/process, and persists outcome/ack; packages/runner/src/platform exists for every supported OS. Today no dispatcher/platform directory/OS lock exists.
9. Provider composition: Claude/Codex process launch, runtime-closure pin, signal/cancel and observation paths have production callers, not only probe/render/stream kernels.
10. Resource/budget/artifact composition: adapterConfirm/adapterFail, budget account/measurement/settlement, provider-slot/resource transitions and createArtifactStore have durable production consumers; today several are internal or test-only.
11. Distribution and host prerequisites: distribution manifest packaging is DONE; real supported-host runs exist for host claims. Off-host stays UNKNOWN.
12. Gate lane: package.json owns shell-neutral test:fault/test:security scripts, both lane tsconfigs compile every discovered file, and tests/fault/foundation plus disaster/Linux/macOS ownership is explicitly preserved.
13. Boundary universe: a versioned production-derived authority/effect registry is public and consumed. The schedule checker’s 10 abstract refs alone do not meet this condition.
14. Every shipping task id for rows 1-13 is named and DONE. REVIEW/WORKING/untracked bytes are not prerequisites.

Cheap probes for the next architect:
- rg with --glob !**/*.test.ts for authenticateCommand(, handleCommandRequest(, createHttpMcpAdapter(, applyImport(, createDataAdapter(, relayMessage(, activateEffect(, consumeActivationGrant(, createArtifactStore(, adapterConfirm( and adapterFail(; each must show a durable consumer, not only its definition.
- Test-Path packages/runner/src/platform and enumerate linux/macos/windows implementation files.
- Plain-Node package-root Object.keys probes for @moe/daemon, @moe/mcp, @moe/import and @moe/runner; Vitest resolution is not loadability evidence.
- Read package.json scripts and run tsc -p for both lane configs; root pnpm typecheck does not reach tests/**.

B. Shared case-manifest contract for each child
Each frozen case carries: caseId, productionBoundaryId, abstractScheduleBoundaryRef, entryPoint, faultClass, phase BEFORE|AFTER|RACE, applicableHost, expectedOutcome REFUSED|UNKNOWN|OUTSIDE_SCOPE, expectedCode, expectedLayer, beforeSnapshotDigest, afterSnapshotOracle, auditOracle, and sourceTaskId. IDs canonicalize actor/effect/resource roles and exclude random ids, timestamps and seed labels. For every production boundary:
- applicableFaults is non-empty;
- all three phases exist;
- caseIds and canonical identities are unique;
- generatedCount equals executedCount and is greater than zero;
- registry minus case ids and cases minus registry both equal empty;
- expectedCode is a member of the production closed vocabulary and expectedLayer is a production layer, never a test-local substitute.
UNKNOWN/OUTSIDE_SCOPE rows still execute a production observation and assert the precise code/layer; no it.skip, it.todo, conditional return, or unreadable result may count as evidence.

C. Required state oracles
1. Unauthorized refusal: compare authoritative aggregate version/event/outbox/decision/effect/resource/provider-slot/budget/audit digests before and after; every mutable delta is zero except the explicitly required redacted rejection audit row.
2. Command/outbox replay: same command/effect id yields one decision, one authoritative effect and one deduplicated delivery; conflict uses its exact code/layer.
3. Budget/resource conservation: sum of available+reserved+active+unknown liability cannot increase, slot/resource holder count never exceeds capacity, and UNKNOWN release cannot fund a successor.
4. Crash boundary: after restart, durable state is whole-or-none, one exact recovery classification/set is offered, and running cannot be inferred from silence.
5. Evidence/provider integrity: byte/digest/closure mismatch is refused before activation/acceptance and no provider output grants verification authority.
6. Hidden-skip guard: generated identities equal observed result identities, counts are non-zero, and any unreadable/aborted schedule is UNKNOWN/FAIL evidence rather than silently omitted.

D. Adversarial mutation allocation
- Authority child: neutralize authentication, capability, stale-epoch and replay guards one at a time; each must redden the row naming that code and layer.
- Integrity child: neutralize canonical-path, runtime-closure and evidence-digest checks; each must redden its production entry-point row.
- Store child: neutralize rollback/expected-version/outbox-inbox dedupe checks without causing syntax failure; whole-or-none or duplicate oracle must red.
- Runtime child: permit grant reuse, UNKNOWN resource release, duplicate provider launch or budget reservation; exact effect/resource/budget oracle must red.
- Parent: remove one case from each manifest and alter one UNKNOWN to PASS; exact-set/non-vacuity and truth-lattice tests must red. Restore every production path by its pre-mutation committed blob hash and rerun green.

No plan may use a helper that recomputes production authority. The production surface supplies result, code, layer and state; tests only snapshot, invoke, and compare.

comments.author: architect-5b5302ee
comments.content:
Fourth planning pass: remove two latent plan defects — gate cycles and accidental root-suite execution — and define the boundary-catalog architecture.

1. Dedicated test tiers, not ordinary *.test.ts
New hostile/process/fault files use *.security.ts and *.fault.ts. Root vitest.config.ts discovers only **/*.test.ts, so these lanes do not silently join every worker's ordinary pnpm test. Existing tests/fault/foundation/*.test.ts remain included in both the ordinary root suite and the dedicated fault config.
- tests/fault/vitest.config.ts includes tests/fault/**/*.test.ts plus tests/fault/**/*.fault.ts, node environment, sequential execution, passWithNoTests false.
- tests/security/vitest.config.ts includes tests/security/**/*.security.ts, node environment, sequential execution, passWithNoTests false.
- focused commands always pass --config; plain vitest run tests/security/... would use the root include and can discover zero files.
- lane tsconfigs include every .ts recursively and extend the strict root base.

2. Corrected lane ordering (the earlier single Child E created a cycle)
G0 Fault-lane infrastructure lands first because committed Foundation tests make the lane non-empty: owns package.json, tests/fault/tsconfig.json, tests/fault/vitest.config.ts; adds test:fault = tsc -p tests/fault/tsconfig.json && vitest run --config tests/fault/vitest.config.ts; verification pnpm test:fault.
S1 Authority-security child then creates tests/security/tsconfig.json, tests/security/vitest.config.ts, authority-cases.ts, authority-matrix.security.ts and verifies via direct tsc + configured Vitest. It does not claim a root security gate yet.
G1 Security-lane wiring runs immediately after S1 and owns only package.json; adds test:security = tsc -p tests/security/tsconfig.json && vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts; verification pnpm test:security.
S2 integrity security and F1/F2 store/runtime fault children then run file-disjoint in their owned subdirectories against the established lanes.
P parent aggregate runs last.
This prevents a green empty security script and gives Linux/macOS/disaster tasks a real test:fault command without waiting for the whole matrix. package.json edits are sequenced, never concurrent.

3. Revised child filenames
- tests/security/transports/authority-cases.ts + authority-matrix.security.ts
- tests/security/integrity/integrity-cases.ts + integrity-matrix.security.ts
- tests/fault/store/store-fault-cases.ts + store-fault-matrix.fault.ts
- tests/fault/runtime/runtime-fault-cases.ts + runtime-fault-matrix.fault.ts
- parent: tests/security/system/security-coverage.security.ts + tests/fault/system/fault-coverage.fault.ts
Case files are imported support, not independently discovered. Each discovered file asserts the imported case count > 0.

4. No-hidden-skip enforcement
The two parent coverage files use the TypeScript compiler API (already a dev dependency) to parse all lane sources and reject actual call expressions using it/test/describe.skip, todo, skipIf or runIf; do not grep text/comments. They assert scanned-file and checked-call counts >0. Runtime generatedCount===executedIdentitySet.size catches conditional early returns and unreadable subprocess results. UNREADABLE/ABORT are explicit evidence classifications, never skipped.

5. Production boundary catalog architecture (avoids reversing package dependencies)
Do not put a hand-authored “whole system” list in testkit or contracts. Contracts may define only the frozen BoundaryDescriptor codec/version. Each production subsystem exports its own catalog from the same module that exposes the entry point or protocol registry. The signed distribution manifest enumerates installed components plus each component catalog digest. The final matrix:
- reads the distribution component set;
- loads every required component catalog from its public production root;
- proves component-set ↔ catalog-set equality and catalog digest equality;
- maps every catalog row to executed cases;
- proves each entry-point/protocol registry’s local exact-set guard in that component’s own package tests.
A new component without a catalog or a catalog without a distribution binding therefore fails closed. Contracts never import consumers, and testkit never authors authority.

BoundaryDescriptor minimum fields: registryVersion, boundaryId, componentId, category AUTHORITY|EXTERNAL_EFFECT|INTEGRITY, publicEntryPoint, abstractScheduleBoundaryRef (one of the schedule checker’s 10 categories), supportedPhases, applicableFaultClasses, stableCodes, stableLayers, hostObservability OBSERVABLE|HOST_DEPENDENT|HOST_MALICIOUS_OUT_OF_SCOPE, and catalogDigest. Governance task ids stay in the acceptance handoff/evidence, not production bytes.

6. Evidence identity
Canonical case identity hashes boundaryId, phase, faultClass, actor/effect/resource role and happens-before edges; it excludes random ids, wall time and seed labels. Each manifest is DEVELOPMENT_ONLY_ENGINEERING_EVIDENCE with confirmatory:false and contains no BENCH identifiers. The verbose lane summary prints component-catalog digests, case-manifest digest, generated/executed counts and explicit UNKNOWN/OUTSIDE_SCOPE counts, but never credentials, raw provider output or physical paths. HEAD/source attribution remains completion evidence rather than a self-referential hash embedded in committed source.

7. Dependency DAG
Production descriptor contract -> subsystem catalogs/real consumer edges -> distribution catalog binding.
In parallel after those land: G0, then S1 and F1/F2 as their production subjects allow; G1 after S1; S2 after its distribution/provider subjects; parent P after G1+S1+S2+F1+F2 plus disaster/Linux/macOS/JetBrains/distribution tasks DONE.
No child edits tests/fault/foundation, tests/fault/disaster-restore, tests/fault/linux or tests/fault/macos.

CATALOG DECISION
A test-authored whole-system list and a central tools/testkit “authority registry” are both rejected: either can stay green while a production component disappears. The acceptable shape is:
1. @moe/contracts defines only a dependency-free, versioned, bounded descriptor/catalog codec and canonical BYTES. It does not import consumers or hash with Node-only APIs.
2. Every subsystem publishes a frozen LOCAL catalog next to the real public factory/handler/protocol registry and locally proves exact-set equality to that production surface.
3. Distribution tooling computes SHA-256 over canonical catalog bytes, signs the aggregate digest with the installed component manifest, and startup recomputes/compares it before accepting requests or effects.
4. The final matrix loads catalogs only through public production roots and proves distribution-component set = loaded-catalog set = generated-case set = executed-result set.
5. Governance task ids stay in planning/completion evidence, not signed production bytes. Production rows carry only a stable evidence-owner class (SECURITY_MATRIX, FAULT_MATRIX, PLATFORM_CONFORMANCE, DISASTER_RESTORE or SUPPLY_CHAIN).
6. The catalog envelope owns the digest; descriptors do not contain a self-referential digest. Canonical identity excludes source checkout paths, separators, random ids, timestamps and seeds.

Minimum descriptor fields: schemaVersion, componentId, boundaryId, category AUTHORITY|EXTERNAL_EFFECT|INTEGRITY, publicEntryPoint, protocol/operation id, abstract schedule ref, applicable fault classes, supported BEFORE|AFTER|RACE phases, per-fault expected outcome/code/layer vocabulary, host observability, and evidence-owner class. Decode rejects empty/duplicate/unknown/extra-key data with one stable catalog code and CATALOG layer. A semantic field mutation changes canonical bytes; row reordering and Windows/POSIX separators do not.

REMAINING PRODUCTION TASK BLUEPRINTS (create only after searching the board; each is a separate <=5-file, <=8-step slice)
A. Hardening descriptor contract — packages/contracts/src/hardening/hardening-boundary-contract.ts, .js bridge, sibling test, and contracts index. RED exact-key/version/duplicate/empty tests; implement frozen decoder+canonical bytes; root-import test; name the first subsystem-catalog consumer task. Gate: pnpm --filter @moe/contracts typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test.
B. Durable relay consumption — publish @moe/store relayMessage and add a daemon runtime command-relay module/test that calls it against real SQLite. APPLIED must read back event+projection+outbox+inbox atomically; redelivery is ALREADY_APPLIED without reducer rerun; OUTCOME_UNKNOWN never becomes success; exact OUTBOX_RELAY code+layer is preserved. IMPORTANT ORACLE CORRECTION
Production local catalogs declare boundary membership, public subject/observation entry points, ordered stages, required phases/fault classes and CLOSED code/layer vocabularies. 1. Security harness (<=5 files under tests/security/harness/**): frozen case/manifest codec, public-root snapshot collector, delta/redaction oracle, deterministic evidence canonicalizer, and one *.security.ts self-test. It may snapshot/invoke/compare only.
2. Fault orchestration H0 (5 files under tests/fault/harness/**): protocol.ts, child-process.ts, evidence.ts, harness-worker.mjs, harness-selftest.fault.ts. It owns bounded subprocess/cleanup mechanics only and names store/runtime matrix tasks as consumers.

DELEGATED platform/disaster/supply-chain rows require their exact owner manifest/evidence binding and have no local driver. Host-malicious rows require the explicit outside-scope code and no positive claim.
- Represent schedules as DAGs of stable roles: SETUP, ATTACK_OR_FAULT, CROSS_BOUNDARY, ACK_OR_RECEIPT, RECOVER_OR_REPLAY, OBSERVE. BEFORE orders attack before crossing; AFTER crosses before attack but attack precedes receipt/recovery; RACE leaves attack and crossing unordered and deterministically enumerates every topological extension. Sixth planning pass B/2 — fault execution, truth/evidence and safe mutation proof. Continues comment-e8ff5b06a0414d9085289109854df425.

FAULT EXECUTION CONTRACT
- H0 always spawns process.execPath with argv arrays, shell:false and an allowlisted environment. Child emits bounded versioned NDJSON and synchronously marks BOUNDARY_REACHED immediately before crash. Marker missing, malformed/duplicate/out-of-order or >64KiB output, timeout, non-clean cleanup, or boundary never reached is exact HARNESS_* FAIL, never product UNKNOWN.
- Track every child, handle and temp root. Request termination and verify through the shipped platform observer. Raw child.kill is emergency cleanup only; if needed the case fails HARNESS_CLEANUP_UNPROVEN. No /tmp, POSIX quoting, signal-name, chmod or assumed directory-fsync behavior. Use Node path/os APIs; volatile time is only a timeout and never identity/evidence.
- Use real on-disk project DBs. BEFORE/AFTER crash workers wrap the PUBLIC operation; RACE uses two independent Node processes and deterministic AB/BA/simultaneous barrier releases. Reopen through public SqliteEventStore, replay the identical identity, and assert the whole-or-none event+decision+outbox+projection+inbox tuple.
- Raw SQLite is supplementary only for integrity_check, foreign_key_check and internal row counts; production reopen supplies business classification/code/layer. WAL checkpoint remains a production prerequisite until a public checkpoint entry point/catalog exists.
- Outbox lost-ack uses two real production consumers and two DBs: receiver durably applies then drops response; retry returns ALREADY_APPLIED and one downstream authoritative event/effect. A canned success port is forbidden.
- Runtime fixture provider is a real child launched through the production platform adapter. Modes die/hang/truncate/malformed/duplicate/reorder/ignore-cancel prove adapter/process/stream robustness only, not vendor behavior. Durable effect/platform observation remains authority; PID silence never proves death.
- No physical start before committed activation; one grant consumption and <=1 authoritative launch/registration/invocation. Post-commit unproven registration is SUSPECT/UNKNOWN and never auto-relaunched. Cancellation must land in one exact production reconciliation arm.
- UNKNOWN resource release/measurement never funds a successor, artifact or settlement; assert capacity and available+reserved+committed+unknown-liability conservation. Artifact faults wrap real Node CAS operations; production verify/delete decides, and REFS_UNCERTAIN/PRESENT never unlinks.
- Poison injected by harness (reducer throw/thenable, adapter throw/malformed response, bad measurement, corrupt provider bytes, I/O error) must emerge from the composed public surface with stable production code/layer or fail the test; the harness cannot translate it.
- F1 excludes backup/restore/slot-switch. F2 owns portable/common Node and Windows rows only. Linux/macOS/disaster tests remain their owners and are joined by exact boundary/evidence identity. Off-host is NOT_OBSERVED with truth UNKNOWN, not OUTSIDE_SCOPE. Harness failure is FAIL. Host-malicious behavior alone is OUTSIDE_SCOPE. No skip or conditional return.

TRUTH AND EVIDENCE
Keep three axes separate:
1. assertionVerdict PASS|FAIL — did observation match the case;
2. production truthClass — use the closed production vocabulary;
3. scopeDisposition IN_SCOPE|OUTSIDE_SCOPE.
A test may pass because the system stayed fail-closed UNKNOWN, but its permitted claim remains UNKNOWN/RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, never “effect did not occur.” Unsupported current host is UNKNOWN, not outside scope. OUTSIDE_SCOPE requires an explicit design/catalog scopeRef and OUT_OF_SCOPE_HOST_EFFECT_UNKNOWN. Summaries never roll UNKNOWN/outside scope into positive counts.

Emit canonical moe-security-fault-evidence/1 JSONL only under an automatically cleaned temp evidence root. Manifest binds ONE frozen source commit plus design, benchmark, distribution, component-catalog, schedule and case-manifest digests from that same basis, environment versions, declared/generated/executed/assertion/UNKNOWN/outside counts and a root digest. Case records bind case identity, boundary/phase/fault/happens-before, independent expectation, observed exact refusal, before/after structured summaries+digests, effect count, audit/redaction and assertion ids. Exclude absolute paths, wall time, PIDs, secrets and raw provider bytes. Require declared=generated=executed (including UNKNOWN/outside rows), unique ids and nonzero every required dimension. Cleanup failure fails the lane. Print only digests, counts and code-layer histograms. No evidence or corpus file is committed, and this task never generates or views confirmatory corpus bytes.

MUTATION SAFETY PREREQUISITE
The final task cannot transiently edit unowned production paths in the shared checkout. Before submission, either:
(a) land an isolated mutation-runner task (<=5 files in @moe/testkit) that archives the exact frozen commit into the approved runtime-isolated temp root, applies one exact compile-valid mutant, runs the named public-root case, rejects compile/unrelated failures, cleans, and records intended killed case ids; task-05ce is its named consumer; or
(b) grant task-05ce an explicit mutation-only scope amendment plus exclusive Moe resource leases for every target file.
Without (a) or (b), the epic-required production-surface mutation proof remains impossible and this task stays blocked. No sibling Git worktree, reset, checkout or stash is allowed.

Required compile-valid mutants: wrong refusal layer while outcome still refuses; replay treated fresh; expected-version/lease/epoch fence bypass; duplicate effect/grant/launch; UNKNOWN release or budget liability made available; artifact ref returned before persistence or UNCERTAIN deletion; provider timeout/unverifiable receipt accepted or retried; GO_ACTIVATE before quiesce/import; secret detail leak or missing/double audit; removed case/seed/race order; UNKNOWN/outside-scope promoted to positive PASS. Every mutant must be killed by its intended named assertion; syntax/typecheck failure and unrelated red do not count. Restore/cleanup is hash-verified.

FINAL PARENT PLAN SHAPE (still 2 files, 7 steps)
1. Admission/freeze: verify all named production, platform, restore, catalog, lane, testkit-publication and mutation-runner tasks DONE; public-root/runtime consumer probes; exact hashes; no confirmatory access.
2. RED security aggregate for catalog/child/case/execution exact-set equality, stage precedence, snapshot/delta/redaction and truth/scope axes.
3. RED fault aggregate for catalog/schedule/owner exact-set equality, subprocess protocol, whole-or-none/effect/conservation and host routing.
4. Minimal aggregate wiring only; any production failure opens a prerequisite defect rather than patching outside owned paths or weakening expectations.
5. Run isolated compile-valid mutations plus in-memory removed-case/seed/race/UNKNOWN->PASS mutations; require intended named red, restore exact hashes, then green.
6. One final verification: baseline/HEAD path-attributed repo failures, then exact pnpm test:fault && pnpm test:security; owned lanes exit 0 and foreign red is disclosed verbatim.
7. Record exact frozen-source stdout/digests/counts with UNKNOWN/outside scope separate. No committed generated evidence and GO_QUIESCE/GO_ACTIVATE remain separate.

Focused child and -t replay commands are development evidence only. Completion verification remains exactly pnpm test:fault && pnpm test:security.

ONE BASIS, NEVER STITCHED
Before edits, record B=git rev-parse HEAD, require owned paths clean, capture porcelain-v2 plus hashes for every foreign dirty path, and run foreground pnpm typecheck + pnpm test as the path-attributed baseline. Logs live only under os.tmpdir keyed by B. This is preflight evidence capture, not an extra implementation gate.

After TDD and explicit-path commit, freeze S=HEAD and T=HEAD^{tree}. Acquire/coordinate a source-freeze resource while delegated receipts and the final gate are collected. If HEAD advances, fail EVIDENCE_SOURCE_CHANGED and recollect everything at the new source; never reset, amend or combine bases.

Every local/delegated result binds the exact vector:
sourceCommit S; sourceTree T; design and benchmark hashes; distribution-manifest digest; aggregate/local catalog digests; security/fault case-set digests; package.json and lockfile digests; security/fault config digests; Node/pnpm versions; exact verification command.
Any mismatch invalidates the whole affected receipt. Matching fields from two receipts may not be salvaged into one artificial basis.

DELEGATED OWNER RECEIPTS
Linux, macOS, disaster-restore and supply-chain owners run their exact suites on clean checkouts of S and emit canonical redacted receipts outside the repository containing:
- schema/version, owner task id, exact delegated boundary-id set;
- the full basis vector;
- host platform/arch/OS build and clean-tree digest;
- exact command/exit code, generated/executed set digest+count;
- per-boundary PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|OUTSIDE_SCOPE with exact production code/layer and truth/scope;
- stdout/stderr digest plus bounded redacted tail;
- trusted issuer/attestation and canonical receipt digest.
Use an existing public evidence-receipt verifier. If no production verifier can authenticate the issuer/basis, that verifier is a prerequisite; a test must not trust JSON because its fields look right.

Sort verified receipts by owner,boundaryId,digest; only byte-identical duplicates dedupe. Conflicting duplicates fail. Store the temporary bundle only at a deterministic os.tmpdir path outside the repo; aggregates never readdir-discover evidence. Verify canonical bytes/attestation/artifact hashes independently, calculate one bundle digest, and clean after recording output. Nothing is staged.

Required disaster/supply-chain rows fail the aggregate on missing/unverifiable/cross-basis evidence. Linux/macOS may remain IN_SCOPE+UNKNOWN only where the production catalog explicitly permits off-host evidence; GA policy may instead mark them required. A matching-host attested receipt can be consumed on another host only when its complete basis is S. Same-user malicious-host rows remain OUTSIDE_SCOPE/OUT_OF_SCOPE_HOST_EFFECT_UNKNOWN and cannot be upgraded by a receipt.

Recommended stable federation failure vocabulary at layer EVIDENCE_FEDERATION:
RECEIPT_MISSING, RECEIPT_UNVERIFIABLE, SOURCE_COMMIT_MISMATCH, SOURCE_TREE_MISMATCH, CATALOG_MISMATCH, CASESET_MISMATCH, DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH, CONFIG_MISMATCH, COMMAND_MISMATCH, HOST_MISMATCH, RECEIPT_CONFLICT, SOURCE_CHANGED, STORAGE_SCOPE_INVALID.
These are harness/evidence classifications, never substitutes for the inner production refusal. Every affected capability claim remains UNKNOWN; any attempted positive claim makes the test red.

SHARED TREE AND BASELINE->HEAD
No worktree/checkout/stash/reset/clean/merge or broad staging. Delegated runners use independent clean CI clones, not sibling worktrees created by this task. A local immutable snapshot, if policy-approved for mutation only, is git-archive extraction under the approved runtime temp root and is deleted; otherwise missing proof stays UNKNOWN.

At final verification step:
1. Re-run repo-wide pnpm typecheck and pnpm test in the shared checkout.
2. Normalize failing paths to Git-relative NFC forward-slash form. Unparseable red is UNATTRIBUTED_GATE_FAILURE, never silently foreign.
3. Compute (HeadPaths - BasePaths) intersect exactOwnedPaths; require empty, and require no baseline failure under owned paths. Disclose remaining foreign failures verbatim.
4. Verify task commit path list contains only exact owned paths; owned paths are clean; status/grep finds no generated evidence, corpus, transcript, mutant or scratch file.
5. Then run LAST, with no edits afterward: pnpm test:fault && pnpm test:security. No -t, seed/host override or alternate receipt basis.
Both legs recompute S/T/basis and use the same receipt bundle; a HEAD change between legs fails. Output prints S/T, catalog/bundle/case digests, generated/executed counts and required/verified/UNKNOWN/outside counts, without secrets or paths. Exit 0 proves only the matrix at this basis; permitted off-host UNKNOWN is reported as UNKNOWN, never platform/GA PASS.

CONFIRMATORY SEPARATION
This task produces DEVELOPMENT_ONLY engineering evidence with confirmatory:false only. It never creates, views, seals or references confirmatory BENCH corpus bytes. The later independent confirmatory-corpus task owns seal-after-implementation-freeze. Do not add a confirmatory manifest or separate harness basis here; all engineering rows bind the one submitted source commit S.

Keep independently versioned:
1. moe-boundary-catalog/1 (production authority);
2. moe-hostile-case-manifest/1 (test obligations, DEVELOPMENT_ONLY, confirmatory:false);
3. moe-hostile-observation/1;
4. moe-hostile-shard-receipt/1;
5. moe-delegated-owner-receipt/1;
6. moe-hostile-aggregate/1;
plus separate moe-hostile-case-identity/1 and canonical-json/1 versions.
All are bounded exact-key null-prototype/NFC records with sorted unique IDs, lowercase full SHA-256 and frozen normalized output. Unknown field => SHAPE_INVALID; unknown version => SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED. No “future” bag or permissive semver.

Compatibility is explicit and asymmetric through a closed pure upcaster table. Upcasting old data is diagnostic only and cannot invent a boundary/case/code/layer/digest/source/count, fill observations, or turn UNKNOWN/outside into VERIFIED. Incomplete semantics => HOSTILE_UPCAST_INCOMPLETE; rerun is required for current PASS. Shape/meaning changes bump that schema; identity-field changes bump identity version and invalidate all receipts; canonicalization changes invalidate every digest. Catalog data/vocabulary changes alter catalog/protocol digest even without a schema bump.

COUNT/DRIFT RULES
Pin literal EXPECTED_CASE_COUNT and exact ID set/digest per shard plus literal aggregate shard table/total. Never derive expected from generated/runtime data. A reduction requires a reviewed retirement ledger with old/new catalog digests, reason and replacement IDs; rename uses supersedes. New boundary => CASE_COVERAGE_MISSING; removed expected boundary => CATALOG_BOUNDARY_MISSING; same ID/changed descriptor => DESCRIPTOR_DRIFT. Structural drift is FAIL, not UNKNOWN. Receipt freshness exact-matches source/tree, document/distribution/catalog/protocol/manifest/harness/registry/toolchain/host/config/command bases; readable stale data is still UNKNOWN/nonzero.

Diagnostics print one deterministic HOSTILE_SHARD_RESULT line and sorted HOSTILE_FINDING lines with stable code/layer/subject/expected/observed/action. Never print paths, PIDs, times, secrets, raw bytes or truncated hashes. An expected product UNKNOWN may exist inside a structurally verified shard only when exact code/layer/zero-authority behavior and literal unknown count are pinned.
